topic: AI basics: why Claude can give a different answer to the same question
post:
Asked Claude the same question twice and got two different answers? 🎲
That's not a bug. Here's why, in plain English.

AI writes its answer one small piece at a time, choosing what comes next as it goes.

There's a setting behind the scenes called "temperature" that controls how much randomness goes into those choices. Anthropic's glossary explains it simply:

🔥 Higher temperature: more creative, more varied answers
❄️ Lower temperature: more predictable, "most likely" answers

And even at the lowest setting, Anthropic says the results still won't be fully identical every time.

So how do you get consistent results? 👇

Be specific about what you want. Clear instructions leave less room for variety.

Try this:
"Summarize this report in exactly 5 bullets. Each bullet under 15 words. Start with the biggest risk."

The tighter the instructions, the more alike the answers.

Why it matters:
Different answers are great for brainstorming. For work that needs to match every time, like a weekly report, give Claude a clear format. 💡
